name: pagehide, visibilitychange and unload
plain: Events that tell a page it is being hidden, left or closed so it can save state or send a last report.
meaning: visibilitychange and pagehide are the reliable last chance for a final send. unload is being retired: Chrome is deprecating it with a Permissions-Policy and completing the change in late 2026. beforeunload is unreliable on mobile.

access.persistence: Fires once at exit or tab hide
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

chrome.note: unload is being phased out in Chrome 154 to 155

limits.headline: Can tell a page when you hide or leave it, so it can send a report
limits.user_action: You switch tabs, close the tab or leave the page
can: Know when you hide or leave a page
Send a final report, such as time spent, through other tools
cannot: Always run, since phones and Chrome may skip the unload event
Keep the page running after it closes
See what you do on the next page
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge limit the unload event. Safari and Firefox run it more often.

story.what_it_is: Events that tell a page it is being hidden or closed, so it can save and send a last report.

marketing.name: Page Lifecycle API
marketing.pitch: Chrome documents events like visibilitychange that tell pages when to save state or send last data.

story.for_you: You never see it. When you switch tabs or close the page, the page gets a short warning. It uses that moment to save your work or send a last report. Old unload events are being retired.
story.for_makers: Pages die with little notice, especially on phones. Hidden and pagehide are the reliable last chance to send data. Games and editors use them to save progress, and analytics use them to finish counting time on page.

use_cases.example: An online editor saves your draft the moment you switch tabs, so nothing is lost if the browser crashes.
A browser game pauses and saves your state when you switch tabs, and sends progress to the server.
A video site sends your watch position when you leave, so you can resume later.
An analytics script sends your time on page when the tab becomes hidden.
A live stream pauses the video feed to save data when you hide the tab, and resumes when you return.
An ad tag stops counting visible time when the page goes into the background.

risks: Sends data at a moment you cannot stop

technical_bounds: unload does not fire reliably on mobile or in bfcache
beforeunload prompt requires a user gesture on the page
Chrome deprecation of unload completes about Chrome 154 to 155 (Sep to Oct 2026)
Only about 100s of ms of work is safe

history.change: Deprecation completes by default (Sep to Oct 2026 per Chrome plan)
